title: Instantaneous Velocity of a Falling Object
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A stone dropped from a high cliff falls s(t) = 16t^2 feet in t seconds. Compute the average velocity over the time interval [2, 2+h], and determine the instantaneous velocity at t = 2 seconds.

steps.title: Set up the Position Values
steps.explanation: Evaluate the position function at the base time t = 2 and at the elapsed time t = 2+h.
steps.why: Evaluation of position at both endpoints is prerequisite for average velocity.

steps.title: Calculate the Average Velocity Difference Quotient
steps.explanation: Compute displacement Delta s over elapsed time h, factoring out h from the numerator.
steps.why: Average velocity is displacement divided by elapsed time.

steps.title: Take the Limit as Elapsed Time Approaches Zero
steps.explanation: Let h approach 0 in the simplified rate expression to find the instantaneous rate of change.
steps.why: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time limit of average velocity as elapsed time approaches zero.
